description: Teacher metadata for every branch, by set: backward branches give the obstacle, why it blocks MAIN, the evidence the five questions collect (rationale) and whether the standard is exact or supporting; forward branches give the progression type, direct or nearest related, the new demand, and (FORWARD 2) how it builds on FORWARD 1. plus_standard is true when the branch's standard is a Common Core (+) standard; this happens in some core-strand sets (their FORWARD 2) as well as in the advanced strand. The same fields are in each set file under sections[].branch.

sets.target_skill: Write, test, and repair a precise definition of a circle, based on the undefined notions of point, plane, and distance

branches.skill: Use the center, radius, and diameter of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect a circle with one fixed distance from a center. Why it matters: that fixed distance is the whole definition of a circle. Evidence: decides from distances whether points are on, inside, or outside a circle.

branches.skill: Find the distance from a center to points on a grid
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot decide which points are a given distance from a center. Why it matters: a circle is exactly the points of a plane at one distance from its center. Evidence: computes distances from a center and compares them.

branches.skill: Test definitions of circle vocabulary with counterexamples
branches.new_demand: Test a proposed definition of a circle or circle part by finding a counterexample (a figure that fits the wording but is not the intended figure) and repair it.

branches.skill: Write precise definitions of circle parts from the definition of a circle
branches.new_demand: Write precise definitions of new circle figures (chord, diameter, semicircle, interior, concentric circles) using only the definition of a circle and earlier terms.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 tests circle definitions with counterexamples; FORWARD 2 writes new definitions that must survive that test.

sets.target_skill: Write, test, and repair a precise definition of an angle (two rays with a common endpoint), and connect degree measure to distance around a circular arc

branches.skill: See an angle as two rays with a common endpoint, measured by an arc
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student thinks of an angle as a corner or a size instead of two rays with a common endpoint. Why it matters: the precise definition of an angle, and of degree measure by arcs, depend on this view. Evidence: names vertex and sides and converts between fractions of a circle and degrees.

branches.skill: Identify rays and their endpoints
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student mixes up rays with lines or segments, or misreads which letter is the endpoint. Why it matters: an angle is defined as two rays with a common endpoint. Evidence: names rays from pictures and notation and identifies their endpoints.

branches.skill: Define angle relationships from the definition of an angle
branches.new_demand: Write precise definitions of angle relationships (adjacent, vertical, linear pair, bisector) from the definition of an angle, and test them.

branches.skill: Prove angle facts from the angle definitions
branches.new_demand: Use the definitions of angle relationships as reasons in short proofs and computations.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the definitions written there are the reasons used in these proofs.

sets.target_skill: Write, test, and apply a precise definition of a line segment using betweenness (distance along a line)

branches.skill: Identify points, lines, rays, and segments
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student mixes up a line, a ray, and a segment. Why it matters: the definition of a segment separates it from lines and rays. Evidence: names figures and counts their endpoints.

branches.skill: Find distances between points on a number line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use distances along a line. Why it matters: betweenness, and so the definition of a segment, is stated with distances along a line. Evidence: finds distances on a number line and tests betweenness.

branches.skill: Define figures built from segments
branches.new_demand: Write precise definitions of new figures (ray, midpoint, triangle, congruent segments, segment bisector) from the definition of a segment.

branches.skill: Test segment-based definitions with counterexamples
branches.new_demand: Find counterexamples to imprecise segment-based definitions and repair them.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the definitions written there are tested against counterexamples.

sets.target_skill: Write, repair, and apply a precise definition of perpendicular lines

branches.skill: Recognize perpendicular lines and right angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot tell perpendicular lines from lines that merely cross. Why it matters: the definition names exactly the right-angle relationship. Evidence: classifies lines and right angles in words and situations.

branches.skill: Find the other angles when two lines cross
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that one right angle forces all four angles to be right angles. Why it matters: the definition of perpendicular lines names one right angle; the others follow from angle pairs. Evidence: finds all four angles from one and uses vertical angles and linear pairs.

branches.skill: Prove consequences of the definition of perpendicular lines
branches.new_demand: Write a proof that derives angle facts from the definition of perpendicular lines, instead of stating the definition.

branches.skill: Reason about perpendicular lines with a third line, in a plane and in space
branches.new_demand: Reason about relationships among THREE lines that involve perpendicularity, including whether a plane statement remains true in space.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 proves facts about one pair of perpendicular lines; FORWARD 2 extends the reasoning to a third line and tests it in space.

sets.target_skill: Write, repair, and apply a precise definition of parallel lines (coplanar lines that do not intersect)

branches.skill: Recognize parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot tell parallel lines from other pairs of lines. Why it matters: the definition names exactly the non-intersecting coplanar pair. Evidence: classifies pairs of lines and sides in words and situations.

branches.skill: Decide whether two lines in the coordinate plane intersect
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot show that two lines have no common point. Why it matters: checking "do not intersect" is half of the definition of parallel lines. Evidence: solves for intersections or shows that none exist.

branches.skill: Visualize lines and planes in a box
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot picture lines that never meet but are not in one plane. Why it matters: the plane condition in the definition exists because of skew lines. Evidence: identifies parallel and skew edges of a box.

branches.skill: Prove that lines are parallel from angle facts
branches.new_demand: Use angle facts with a transversal to prove that two lines are parallel, instead of only applying the definition.

branches.skill: Use the parallel postulate
branches.new_demand: Use the parallel postulate (uniqueness of the parallel) as a reason.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the proof that a ∥ b and b ∥ c imply a ∥ c already uses the postulate; FORWARD 2 states and applies it directly.

sets.target_skill: Describe a transformation as a function on points: apply its rule to inputs, find preimages, and write rules in function notation

branches.skill: Evaluate a rule for a given input
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not treat a rule as an input-output machine. Why it matters: a transformation is a function whose inputs and outputs are points. Evidence: evaluates rules, works backward to an input, and recognizes the one-output condition.

branches.skill: Apply coordinate rules for translations, reflections, and rotations
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot move a single point by a described transformation. Why it matters: writing a transformation as a function starts from moving individual points. Evidence: applies translation, reflection, and rotation rules to points.

branches.skill: Read and locate ordered pairs in all four quadrants
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reverses x and y or misreads signs. Why it matters: every input and output of a transformation is an ordered pair. Evidence: reads and places points with negative coordinates.

branches.skill: Compose two transformations and write one rule
branches.new_demand: Compose two transformation functions, write the composite rule, and recognize that order can matter.

branches.skill: Find the inverse of a transformation
branches.new_demand: Find the inverse of a transformation function and decide when no inverse exists.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the inverse is the transformation whose composition with T is the identity.

sets.target_skill: Decide, with coordinates and examples, whether a transformation preserves distance and angle measure

branches.skill: Find the distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the distance between two points. Why it matters: checking whether a transformation preserves distance means comparing distances before and after. Evidence: uses the Pythagorean Theorem (and horizontal distance) to find lengths.

branches.skill: Know that rigid motions keep lengths and angle measures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know which properties rigid motions keep. Why it matters: comparing transformations depends on knowing what a rigid motion preserves. Evidence: states and applies the preserved properties.

branches.skill: Classify transformations as rigid motions, similarity transformations, or neither
branches.new_demand: Sort transformations into three classes (rigid, similarity, neither) by testing what happens to distances and angles.

branches.skill: Prove with variables that a transformation preserves or scales every distance
branches.new_demand: Prove the classification for ALL pairs of points with variables, and explain why examples alone cannot prove it.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 classifies transformations with specific points; FORWARD 2 proves the general claim algebraically.

sets.target_skill: Describe every rotation and reflection that carries a given rectangle, parallelogram, or trapezoid onto itself

branches.skill: Identify lines of symmetry of figures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find lines of symmetry. Why it matters: every reflection that carries a figure onto itself is across a line of symmetry. Evidence: counts and identifies lines of symmetry of familiar figures.

branches.skill: Know the side and angle properties of parallelograms, rectangles, and trapezoids
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know which sides and angles of these quadrilaterals match. Why it matters: a symmetry must send each side and angle to a congruent one. Evidence: states side, angle, and diagonal properties of each figure.

branches.skill: Rotate points by 90° and 180° about the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot predict where a rotation sends a point. Why it matters: deciding whether a rotation carries a figure onto itself means checking where its vertices go. Evidence: rotates points by 90° and 180° with the coordinate rules.

branches.skill: Use a symmetry to deduce congruent parts of the figure
branches.new_demand: Use the rigid motion that carries a figure onto itself to deduce which of its sides, angles, and diagonals are congruent.

branches.skill: Combine symmetries and identify a figure from its symmetries
branches.new_demand: Compose two symmetries into one transformation and work backward from a list of symmetries to the figure.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 uses one symmetry at a time; FORWARD 2 combines symmetries and reverses the question (from symmetries to figure).

sets.target_skill: Describe every rotation and reflection that carries a regular polygon onto itself

branches.skill: Find the angle of a fraction of a full turn
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot turn "one nth of a turn" into degrees. Why it matters: the rotations of a regular n-gon are multiples of 360° ÷ n. Evidence: converts fractions of a turn to degrees.

branches.skill: Recognize regular polygons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know that regular means equal sides AND equal angles. Why it matters: the symmetries of a regular polygon come from its equal sides and angles. Evidence: identifies regular polygons and names them by number of sides.

branches.skill: Find lines of symmetry of regular polygons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find all lines of symmetry. Why it matters: each reflection that carries a regular polygon onto itself is across a line of symmetry. Evidence: counts and locates lines of symmetry.

branches.skill: Work backward from a symmetry to the regular polygon
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the polygon (or its full set of symmetries) from one given symmetry.

branches.skill: Combine symmetries of a regular polygon
branches.new_demand: Compose two symmetries of a regular polygon and track where a vertex ends up.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 finds the polygon from one symmetry; FORWARD 2 combines two symmetries into one.

sets.target_skill: Define a reflection precisely using the perpendicular bisector, and use the definition to locate images and lines of reflection

branches.skill: Find the midpoint of a horizontal or vertical segment
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the point halfway between two points. Why it matters: a line of reflection passes through the midpoint of each segment PP′. Evidence: finds midpoints on number lines and of horizontal and vertical segments.

branches.skill: Recognize perpendicular lines on a grid
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot tell perpendicular directions on a grid. Why it matters: the definition of a reflection is stated with a perpendicular bisector. Evidence: recognizes perpendicular lines by their direction.

branches.skill: Reflect points with coordinate rules
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot apply a reflection to a point. Why it matters: checking the definition against an example requires the image point. Evidence: applies reflection rules.

branches.skill: Find lines of reflection and images in slanted, non-axis cases
branches.new_demand: Use the definition when the line of reflection is slanted (not an axis or a grid line).

branches.skill: Prove from the definition that reflections keep lengths
branches.new_demand: Prove from the definition that a reflection preserves the length of a segment.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 applies the definition in slanted cases; FORWARD 2 uses the same definition to prove that lengths are kept.

sets.target_skill: Define a translation precisely using parallel segments of equal length and direction, and use the definition to locate images

branches.skill: Recognize parallel segments on a grid
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot recognize parallel directions on a grid. Why it matters: the definition of a translation is stated with parallel segments. Evidence: recognizes and builds parallel segments.

branches.skill: Translate points with coordinate rules
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot apply a translation to a point. Why it matters: checking the definition against an example requires the image point. Evidence: applies translation rules.

branches.skill: Use the definition with points and their images
branches.new_demand: Use the definition to find images and preimages from one point and its image.

branches.skill: Prove from the definition that translations keep lengths
branches.new_demand: Prove from the definition that a translation preserves length, including the case on one line.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the parallel, equal segments used there are the facts the proof uses.

sets.target_skill: Define a rotation precisely using a center, an angle, and circles, and use the definition to locate images and possible centers

branches.skill: Describe turns in degrees, clockwise and counterclockwise
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is unsure of the size and direction of a turn. Why it matters: a rotation is defined by an angle and a direction. Evidence: converts turns to degrees and tracks clockwise and counterclockwise.

branches.skill: Points on a circle are the same distance from its center
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that a rotation moves points along circles about the center. Why it matters: the definition of a rotation keeps the distance to the center. Evidence: uses equal distances from a center.

branches.skill: Rotate points 90°, 180°, and 270° about the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rotate a point with the coordinate rules. Why it matters: the definition is checked against coordinate examples. Evidence: applies the 90°, 180°, and 270° rules.

branches.skill: Rotate about a center that is not the origin
branches.new_demand: Apply the rotation definition when the center is not the origin (positions relative to the center).

branches.skill: Find the center and angle of a rotation from points and their images
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the center and angle of a rotation from points and their images.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 rotates about any given center; FORWARD 2 reverses the task and finds the center and angle.

sets.target_skill: Draw the image of a given figure under a given rotation, reflection, or translation

branches.skill: Plot and read points in all four quadrants
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot place points from coordinates. Why it matters: drawing an image means plotting its vertices. Evidence: plots and reads points with negative coordinates.

branches.skill: Find image points with coordinate rules
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find where each vertex goes. Why it matters: an image figure is drawn vertex by vertex. Evidence: applies the rules to vertices.

branches.skill: Count the distance from a point to a horizontal or vertical line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot measure how far a point is from a reflection line. Why it matters: a reflected point is the same distance from the line on the other side. Evidence: finds distances to horizontal and vertical lines.

branches.skill: Draw the image under a sequence of two transformations
branches.new_demand: Draw the image after a sequence of two transformations, applied in the given order.

branches.skill: Draw rotations and reflections off the grid with compass, protractor, and straightedge
branches.new_demand: Leave the grid: draw rotation and reflection images with compass, protractor, and straightedge for slanted lines and non-right angles.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 sequences grid transformations; FORWARD 2 carries out the same transformations without coordinates, using tools.

sets.target_skill: Specify a sequence of rigid transformations that carries a given figure onto a given congruent figure

branches.skill: Understand congruence as the result of one rigid motion
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect congruent figures with a motion that carries one onto the other. Why it matters: a sequence is built one rigid motion at a time. Evidence: names the single motion relating two figures.

branches.skill: Find images with coordinate rules for sequences
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot check a proposed sequence point by point. Why it matters: a sequence is verified by tracking each vertex. Evidence: computes images under each kind of rigid motion.

branches.skill: Read the orientation (clockwise or counterclockwise order) of a triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not notice when a figure has been flipped. Why it matters: a sequence must include a reflection exactly when the orientation is reversed. Evidence: reads orientation and predicts the effect of each rigid motion on it.

branches.skill: Use the fewest transformations and justify
branches.new_demand: Replace a sequence by an equivalent shorter one and justify the fewest transformations needed, using orientation.

branches.skill: Specify a similarity sequence: a dilation and rigid motions
branches.new_demand: Add a dilation: specify a similarity sequence that carries a figure onto a similar, larger or smaller figure.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 minimizes rigid sequences; FORWARD 2 extends sequences to similar (not congruent) figures by adding a dilation.

sets.target_skill: Use the geometric description of a rigid motion to predict where a figure goes and which of its measures and relationships stay the same, without coordinates

branches.skill: Know what rigid motions keep: lines, lengths, angles, and parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know which properties survive a rigid motion. Why it matters: predicting the effect of a rigid motion means stating what stays the same. Evidence: states and applies the preserved properties.

branches.skill: Match the vertices and sides of a figure with its image
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot say which part of the image matches which part of the figure. Why it matters: every prediction is about a matching part. Evidence: uses prime notation to match vertices, sides, and angles.

branches.skill: Predict the effect of a sequence of rigid motions
branches.new_demand: Predict the result of a SEQUENCE of rigid motions: orientation, fixed points, and lines that map onto themselves.

branches.skill: Use a rigid motion to conclude that parts of a figure are congruent
branches.new_demand: Turn a known rigid motion into conclusions: name the congruent parts it guarantees and use them.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 predicts what a sequence does; FORWARD 2 uses a rigid motion as the reason that specific parts are congruent.

sets.target_skill: Given two figures, decide whether they are congruent by giving a rigid motion that carries one onto the other or by explaining why no rigid motion can

branches.skill: Recognize congruent figures as images under rigid motions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not link congruence to rigid motions. Why it matters: deciding congruence means finding (or ruling out) such a motion. Evidence: recognizes when figures must be congruent.

branches.skill: Find lengths on a grid with the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compare lengths of slanted sides. Why it matters: equal lengths are needed for a rigid motion to exist. Evidence: computes horizontal, vertical, and slanted lengths.

branches.skill: Decide congruence for figures given by measurements, including curved figures
branches.new_demand: Decide congruence when figures are given by measurements (or are curved), justifying with a motion or an invariant.

branches.skill: Use an established congruence to find unknown parts
branches.new_demand: Use the correspondence from a congruence to set up and solve for unknown sides and angles.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 decides whether figures are congruent; FORWARD 2 starts from a congruence and uses its correspondence.

sets.target_skill: Use the rigid-motion definition to show both directions: a rigid motion between triangles makes all corresponding sides and angles congruent, and congruent corresponding parts give a rigid motion

branches.skill: Read a congruence statement to match corresponding parts
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot match parts from the order of letters. Why it matters: the theorem is about CORRESPONDING parts. Evidence: reads a congruence statement and names corresponding sides and angles.

branches.skill: Rigid motions keep lengths and angle measures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know that rigid motions keep lengths and angles. Why it matters: this is the reason corresponding parts are congruent. Evidence: states and uses the preserved properties.

branches.skill: Move a point onto another and a ray onto another with rigid motions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot plan the motions that place one triangle on another. Why it matters: the converse direction builds a rigid motion step by step. Evidence: chooses a translation, a rotation, and a reflection for given goals.

branches.skill: Find which three corresponding parts are enough
branches.new_demand: Decide which smaller sets of corresponding parts guarantee congruence, with counterexamples for those that do not.

branches.skill: Use congruent triangles to prove a relationship in a figure
branches.new_demand: Prove a relationship in a figure by first proving two triangles congruent and then using corresponding parts.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 finds which parts force congruence; FORWARD 2 uses such a congruence inside a proof.

sets.target_skill: Explain, using rigid motions, why two triangles with two pairs of congruent sides and congruent included angles are congruent

branches.skill: Identify the included angle and included side
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student confuses an included angle with any angle of the triangle. Why it matters: SAS works only for the included angle. Evidence: names included angles and sides and knows which conditions fix a triangle.

branches.skill: Rigid motions map rays, lengths, and angles to equal ones
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot say why a point lands where it does after a motion. Why it matters: each step of the SAS argument is justified by a preserved property. Evidence: uses preserved lengths and angles to locate image points.

branches.skill: Choose a translation, rotation, or reflection to move a point or ray onto a target
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot choose the motion for each step of the argument. Why it matters: the SAS argument is a planned sequence of three motions. Evidence: chooses the motion that achieves each goal.

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent by SAS inside a larger figure
branches.new_demand: Use SAS to prove congruence inside a compound figure, finding the needed parts (shared sides, vertical angles, parallel lines).

branches.skill: Decide whether given information is enough for SAS, and name a missing condition
branches.new_demand: Judge whether given data suffice for SAS and name the exact missing condition, with a reason.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: before using SAS in a proof, decide whether the available data actually satisfy it.

sets.target_skill: Explain, using rigid motions, why two triangles with two pairs of congruent angles and congruent included sides are congruent

branches.skill: Two angles and the included side determine a triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why two angles and the side between them fix a triangle. Why it matters: ASA rests on that fact. Evidence: decides when two angles and a side determine a triangle.

branches.skill: Two different lines meet in at most one point
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know that two different lines cross at most once. Why it matters: ASA locates the third vertex as the single crossing point of two rays. Evidence: counts intersection points of lines.

branches.skill: Rigid motions keep rays and angle measures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use preserved angles to place rays. Why it matters: ASA uses equal angles to put the triangle's sides on top of each other. Evidence: uses preserved angle measures and the uniqueness of a ray at a given angle.

branches.skill: Explain AAS from ASA and the triangle angle sum
branches.new_demand: Derive a new criterion (AAS) from ASA using the triangle angle sum.

branches.skill: Prove congruence with ASA or AAS in overlapping triangles
branches.new_demand: Use ASA/AAS to prove congruence in overlapping and crossing figures, finding shared parts.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 extends ASA to AAS; FORWARD 2 applies both inside figures where the triangles overlap.

sets.target_skill: Explain, using rigid motions, why two triangles with three pairs of congruent sides are congruent

branches.skill: Three side lengths determine a triangle (triangle inequality)
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that three lengths fix a triangle. Why it matters: SSS says exactly that, with rigid motions as the reason. Evidence: uses the triangle inequality and uniqueness from three sides.

branches.skill: Find the points at given distances from two points (two circles)
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate a point from two distances. Why it matters: the SSS argument locates the third vertex this way. Evidence: reasons about where circles about two centers meet.

branches.skill: Rigid motions keep every length
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use preserved lengths to locate image points. Why it matters: the SSS argument relies on DC′ = DC and EC′ = EC. Evidence: states and applies that rigid motions keep lengths.

branches.skill: Explain the Hypotenuse-Leg criterion for right triangles
branches.new_demand: Derive a new criterion for right triangles (HL) by reducing it to SSS with the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Decide which criteria guarantee congruence, with counterexamples
branches.new_demand: Judge which combinations of data are sufficient, justifying "no" with an explicit counterexample.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 adds HL by reducing it to SSS; FORWARD 2 surveys all combinations, proving or refuting each.

sets.target_skill: Prove that vertical angles are congruent

branches.skill: Angles in a linear pair add to 180°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know that a linear pair adds to 180°. Why it matters: every step of the vertical angle proof uses a linear pair. Evidence: finds and uses linear pairs.

branches.skill: Use properties of equality as reasons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name the algebra behind a proof step. Why it matters: the vertical angle proof is two linear pairs plus equality properties. Evidence: names the property that justifies each algebraic step.

branches.skill: Identify vertical angles and linear pairs in a figure
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the vertical and linear-pair angles in a figure. Why it matters: the proof starts by naming them. Evidence: identifies the angle pairs formed by two crossing lines.

branches.skill: Use the vertical angle theorem in multistep proofs
branches.new_demand: Use the vertical angle theorem as one step inside a longer proof with bisectors and several lines.

branches.skill: Prove statements about the bisectors of angles formed by two lines
branches.new_demand: Prove new statements about angle bisectors, and test a converse with a counterexample.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: combines bisectors with linear pairs and vertical angles in new, general statements.

sets.target_skill: Prove that when a transversal crosses parallel lines, alternate interior angles are congruent and corresponding angles are congruent

branches.skill: Name and use angles formed by parallel lines and a transversal
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name the angle pairs or their relationships. Why it matters: the theorems are about these specific pairs. Evidence: names corresponding, alternate interior, and same-side angles and finds their measures.

branches.skill: Vertical angles and linear pairs as reasons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot connect angles at one crossing. Why it matters: each proof links the two crossings with vertical angles or linear pairs. Evidence: gives vertical-angle and linear-pair reasons.

branches.skill: The parallel postulate and the definition of parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the uniqueness of the parallel through a point. Why it matters: the rigid-motion proof depends on it. Evidence: uses the definition of parallel lines and the parallel postulate.

branches.skill: Prove the converse: congruent alternate interior angles make lines parallel
branches.new_demand: Prove the CONVERSE (from congruent angles to parallel lines), which needs an indirect argument.

branches.skill: Use parallel-line theorems to prove the triangle angle sum
branches.new_demand: Apply the parallel-line theorems as tools to prove a triangle theorem.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 proves when lines are parallel; FORWARD 2 uses parallel lines to prove the triangle angle sum.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the points on the perpendicular bisector of a segment are exactly the points equidistant from its endpoints (both directions)

branches.skill: Use the definitions of midpoint and perpendicular bisector
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what the perpendicular bisector is. Why it matters: the theorem is about that line. Evidence: applies the definitions of midpoint and perpendicular bisector.

branches.skill: Use SAS and SSS to prove triangles congruent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot choose a congruence criterion. Why it matters: both directions of the proof use a congruence (SAS, then SSS). Evidence: picks SAS or SSS from given parts.

branches.skill: Corresponding parts of congruent triangles and right angles from a linear pair
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot draw conclusions from a congruence. Why it matters: each proof ends by naming corresponding parts. Evidence: names corresponding parts and the right-angle consequence.

branches.skill: Use the perpendicular bisector to find points equidistant from two points
branches.new_demand: Use the theorem with coordinates to locate points equidistant from two points (equation of the bisector).

branches.skill: Prove that the perpendicular bisectors of a triangle meet at one point
branches.new_demand: Use both directions of the theorem in a new proof: the three perpendicular bisectors are concurrent.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 finds points equidistant from two points; FORWARD 2 extends to three points (the circumcenter) with a proof.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the measures of the interior angles of any triangle add to 180°

branches.skill: Use the angle sum and parallel-line angles informally
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the angle sum or the parallel-line angle facts informally. Why it matters: the proof turns this informal fact into a deduction. Evidence: uses the angle sum and parallel-line angle pairs in calculations.

branches.skill: Angles that form a straight angle add to 180°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that the angles at the parallel line form a straight angle. Why it matters: that is the final step of the proof. Evidence: adds angles that make up a straight angle.

branches.skill: Alternate interior angles of parallel lines are congruent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify the key step of the proof. Why it matters: the new angles at C equal ∠A and ∠B because of this theorem. Evidence: uses alternate interior angles and the parallel postulate.

branches.skill: Prove the exterior angle theorem
branches.new_demand: Prove a new theorem (the exterior angle theorem) that depends on the angle sum.

branches.skill: Generalize the angle sum to polygons
branches.new_demand: Generalize the result with a parameter: the angle sum of an n-sided polygon, by dissection into triangles.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 derives one consequence (exterior angles); FORWARD 2 generalizes the theorem to every polygon.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with SAS or SSS
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot choose or apply a congruence criterion. Why it matters: each proof of the theorem uses SAS or SSS. Evidence: chooses SAS or SSS and states the corresponding parts.

branches.skill: Use the definitions of angle bisector and midpoint
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the auxiliary line's definition as a reason. Why it matters: the proofs depend on the bisector or midpoint giving congruent parts. Evidence: states what a bisector and a midpoint give.

branches.skill: Classify triangles and name legs, base, and base angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know which angles are the base angles. Why it matters: the theorem is about the angles opposite the congruent sides. Evidence: names legs, base, and base angles.

branches.skill: Prove the converse: congruent base angles give congruent sides
branches.new_demand: Prove the converse theorem (from angles to sides), which needs a different congruence criterion (AAS).

branches.skill: Use isosceles triangle theorems in multistep problems and proofs
branches.new_demand: Use the theorem and its converse as steps inside longer calculations and proofs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: both directions of the theorem are used together in multistep reasoning.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to the third side and half as long

branches.skill: Find midpoints of segments in the coordinate plane
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find midpoints, especially with letters. Why it matters: the coordinate proof starts from the two midpoints. Evidence: averages coordinates, including variable coordinates.

branches.skill: Find and compare slopes to decide whether lines are parallel
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot test parallelism with slopes. Why it matters: the coordinate proof shows DE ∥ AB by equal slopes. Evidence: computes and compares slopes.

branches.skill: Find lengths with the distance formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compare the lengths of DE and AB. Why it matters: the "half as long" part needs both lengths. Evidence: finds lengths, including with variables.

branches.skill: Prove lines parallel from congruent alternate interior angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify a parallel conclusion in the synthetic proof. Why it matters: the proof shows BF ∥ AC this way. Evidence: uses the converse to conclude lines are parallel.

branches.skill: Prove that the midpoints of a quadrilateral's sides form a parallelogram
branches.new_demand: Use the midsegment theorem twice inside a new proof about quadrilaterals.

branches.skill: Midsegment triangles: similarity, scale factor, and area
branches.new_demand: Connect the midsegment theorem to similarity: scale factor ½ and the area ratio ¼.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 uses midsegments to prove a parallelogram; FORWARD 2 measures how the midsegment figure compares in size (similarity and area).

sets.target_skill: Prove that the three medians of any triangle meet at one point

branches.skill: Find midpoints, including with variables
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate the endpoints of the medians. Why it matters: every median ends at a midpoint. Evidence: finds midpoints and identifies medians.

branches.skill: Use the midsegment theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not apply the midsegment theorem. Why it matters: the synthetic proof uses it twice. Evidence: uses the theorem for lengths and parallelism.

branches.skill: Find the point a given fraction of the way along a segment
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find a point two-thirds of the way along a segment. Why it matters: the medians meet at the two-thirds point of each. Evidence: computes points at a fractional distance along segments.

branches.skill: Write the equation of a line through two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write a median as a line. Why it matters: the coordinate method shows a point is on each median line. Evidence: writes and checks line equations.

branches.skill: Locate the centroid and use the 2 : 1 ratio
branches.new_demand: Use the concurrency point quantitatively: find the centroid and apply the 2 : 1 division of each median.

branches.skill: Prove that the angle bisectors of a triangle meet at one point
branches.new_demand: Prove a different concurrency theorem (angle bisectors) with the same strategy of two lines meeting and a converse.
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 measures with the centroid; FORWARD 2 proves concurrency of a different set of lines.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent

branches.skill: Alternate interior angles of parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get angle facts from the parallel sides. Why it matters: the proof starts there. Evidence: names alternate interior angles in a parallelogram with a diagonal.

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with ASA
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot complete the congruence step. Why it matters: the proof uses ASA with the diagonal. Evidence: applies ASA and reads the correspondence.

branches.skill: Know the definition of a parallelogram
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what a parallelogram is given to have. Why it matters: the proof may use only the definition (parallel sides). Evidence: states the definition and names opposite sides.

branches.skill: Prove that the diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular
branches.new_demand: Prove and use side-based properties of a special parallelogram (rhombus) that build on the general theorems.

branches.skill: Use opposite sides with coordinates and algebra
branches.new_demand: Use the theorem with coordinates and equations to find vertices and unknown lengths.
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 adds a special case (rhombus); FORWARD 2 applies the theorem with coordinates and algebra.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the opposite angles of a parallelogram are congruent

branches.skill: Same-side interior angles of parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that consecutive angles of a parallelogram are supplementary. Why it matters: one proof of opposite angles uses this twice. Evidence: finds same-side interior angles.

branches.skill: Name opposite and consecutive angles of a quadrilateral
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name opposite angles. Why it matters: the theorem is about them. Evidence: names opposite and consecutive angles.

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with ASA and use corresponding angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the angle conclusion from a congruence. Why it matters: the diagonal proof ends with corresponding angles. Evidence: reads correspondences and names corresponding angles.

branches.skill: Prove angle properties of special parallelograms
branches.new_demand: Use the opposite-angle theorem with consecutive angles in special parallelograms and equations.

branches.skill: Opposite angles and angles of rotation with coordinates
branches.new_demand: Use the 180° rotation symmetry with coordinates to match opposite angles.
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 uses the theorem with special parallelograms; FORWARD 2 connects it to rotation symmetry with coordinates.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other

branches.skill: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are congruent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the earlier theorem. Why it matters: the diagonal proof needs AB = CD. Evidence: uses opposite sides in calculations.

branches.skill: Vertical and alternate interior angles at the crossing of the diagonals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the angle pairs in the diagonal figure. Why it matters: the congruence uses them. Evidence: names vertical and alternate interior angles.

branches.skill: Find the midpoint of a segment and use the definition of bisect
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what "bisect each other" requires. Why it matters: the conclusion is a midpoint statement. Evidence: finds midpoints and states the definition.

branches.skill: Prove that a 180° rotation carries a parallelogram onto itself
branches.new_demand: Connect the theorem to symmetry: prove the 180° rotation property and use it as a new reason.

branches.skill: Use diagonal bisection with coordinates and algebra
branches.new_demand: Use the theorem to locate missing vertices and solve for unknown lengths with algebra.
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 adds symmetry; FORWARD 2 applies the theorem with coordinates and equations.

sets.target_skill: Prove that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram from its opposite sides, opposite angles, or diagonals (the converses)

branches.skill: Converses of the parallel-line angle theorems
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot conclude parallel lines from angles. Why it matters: every converse proof ends by proving sides parallel. Evidence: applies the converse theorems.

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with SSS and SAS
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot reach the needed congruence. Why it matters: each converse proof uses SSS or SAS. Evidence: chooses the criterion.

branches.skill: Angle sum of a quadrilateral
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the quadrilateral angle sum. Why it matters: the opposite-angles converse uses it. Evidence: applies the 360° sum.

branches.skill: Prove that a quadrilateral is a parallelogram using coordinates
branches.new_demand: Apply the converses with coordinates to prove or disprove that four points form a parallelogram.

branches.skill: Decide which conditions are enough to guarantee a parallelogram
branches.new_demand: Judge whether proposed conditions are sufficient, giving a proof or an explicit counterexample.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after using the converses, decide which other conditions do (or do not) work.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the diagonals of a rectangle are congruent, and conversely that a parallelogram with congruent diagonals is a rectangle

branches.skill: Parallelogram properties: opposite sides and consecutive angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the parallelogram properties. Why it matters: both directions rely on them. Evidence: applies opposite sides and consecutive angles.

branches.skill: SAS and SSS with overlapping triangles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot separate the overlapping triangles. Why it matters: both proofs use △ABC and △BAD. Evidence: reads overlapping correspondences.

branches.skill: Use the Pythagorean Theorem for diagonals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find diagonal lengths. Why it matters: the coordinate proof compares diagonal lengths. Evidence: uses the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Decide whether four points form a rectangle
branches.new_demand: Apply the theorem and its converse with coordinates to prove or disprove that a figure is a rectangle.

branches.skill: Prove diagonal properties of rhombuses and squares
branches.new_demand: Prove the diagonal characterizations of the other special parallelograms (rhombus, square).
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 applies the rectangle test with coordinates; FORWARD 2 proves analogous tests for rhombuses and squares.

sets.target_skill: Construct a segment congruent to a given segment with compass and straightedge (and with other tools)

branches.skill: Compare and measure lengths
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect "congruent" with "same length". Why it matters: a copy must have exactly the same length. Evidence: compares and combines lengths.

branches.skill: A compass draws all points at one distance from its center
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know why a compass copies lengths. Why it matters: the construction depends on the arc being at a fixed distance. Evidence: uses the circle definition.

branches.skill: Know rays, segments, and their endpoints
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misreads where the copy must go. Why it matters: the copy starts at the ray's endpoint. Evidence: reads ray and segment notation.

branches.skill: Construct a triangle from three given segments
branches.new_demand: Use segment copying as a tool inside a larger construction (a triangle from three sides).

branches.skill: Decide whether segments can form a triangle, and construct sums and differences
branches.new_demand: Reason about existence: decide when a construction from given lengths is possible, and construct sums and differences.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: asks when the triangle construction succeeds and extends copying to sums and differences.

sets.target_skill: Carry out a formal construction with a tool other than compass and straightedge (paper folding, string, a reflective device, or dynamic geometry software) and explain why the method is exact

branches.skill: Congruent segments have equal lengths
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see that a length can be carried without measuring. Why it matters: every alternative tool carries a fixed length. Evidence: compares and transfers lengths.

branches.skill: A reflection maps a point to its mirror image
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see a fold as a reflection. Why it matters: paper-folding constructions are justified by reflections. Evidence: connects folding with reflection properties.

branches.skill: Choose and justify a method for a construction
branches.new_demand: Choose among tools and justify why a method is an exact construction.

branches.skill: Locate the circumcenter by folding
branches.new_demand: Use folding and string to locate the circumcenter and draw the circumscribed circle.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the justified folding method is applied twice to a triangle.

sets.target_skill: Construct an angle congruent to a given angle with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Measure and draw angles with a protractor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what it means for angles to be congruent. Why it matters: a copy must have the same measure. Evidence: measures and compares angles.

branches.skill: Copy a segment with a compass
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot transfer the lengths the angle copy depends on. Why it matters: copying an angle copies two radii and a chord. Evidence: transfers lengths with a fixed compass.

branches.skill: Arcs and circles in constructions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not read construction arcs as circles. Why it matters: every step uses an arc's center and radius. Evidence: names centers and radii.

branches.skill: Justify why the angle-copy construction works
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction is correct, using a congruence criterion.

branches.skill: Use angle copying to construct a parallel line
branches.new_demand: Use angle copying as a tool for a new construction (a parallel line).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the justified angle copy becomes the key step of the parallel-line construction.

sets.target_skill: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a given segment, and so its midpoint, with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Points equidistant from A and B lie on the perpendicular bisector
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know why the arc crossings lie on the bisector. Why it matters: the construction locates two points of the bisector. Evidence: uses the theorem and its converse.

branches.skill: Know midpoint and perpendicular bisector definitions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is unsure what is being constructed. Why it matters: the result must pass through the midpoint at a right angle. Evidence: applies the definitions.

branches.skill: Arcs with one radius from two centers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student draws arcs that miss each other. Why it matters: the construction needs two crossing points. Evidence: chooses and reasons about radii.

branches.skill: Justify the perpendicular bisector construction
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction produces the perpendicular bisector.

branches.skill: Construct the circumcenter and circumscribed circle of a triangle
branches.new_demand: Use the construction twice to locate a point equidistant from three points (the circumcenter).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the justified construction is repeated for two sides to find the circumcenter.

sets.target_skill: Construct the bisector of a given angle with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Know the definition of an angle bisector
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is unsure what the bisector is. Why it matters: the construction must split the angle evenly. Evidence: applies the definition.

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with SSS
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot see why the construction works. Why it matters: SSS is the reason. Evidence: applies SSS in the figure.

branches.skill: Measure angles with a protractor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect bisecting with halving the measure. Why it matters: a check of the construction compares the two halves. Evidence: measures and halves angles.

branches.skill: Justify the angle bisector construction
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction is correct, using SSS.

branches.skill: Construct special angles and the incenter by bisecting
branches.new_demand: Combine angle bisection with other constructions to create new angles and the incenter.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the justified bisector becomes a tool for new constructions.

sets.target_skill: Construct the line perpendicular to a given line through a given point, on the line or not on it

branches.skill: Know the definition of perpendicular lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is unsure of the goal. Why it matters: the constructed line must form right angles. Evidence: applies the definition.

branches.skill: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a segment
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot complete the final step. Why it matters: both perpendicular constructions end with a perpendicular bisector. Evidence: uses that construction.

branches.skill: Recognize perpendicular lines in figures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot recognize perpendicularity. Why it matters: needed to check the result. Evidence: identifies perpendicular lines.

branches.skill: Construct an altitude of a triangle and use it for area
branches.new_demand: Use the perpendicular construction in a triangle (altitudes, including outside the triangle).

branches.skill: Construct a square on a given segment
branches.new_demand: Combine perpendicular constructions with segment copying to build a polygon.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: uses perpendiculars at both ends of a segment, plus copying, to construct a square.

sets.target_skill: Construct the line through a given point parallel to a given line, with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Copy an angle with compass and straightedge
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot copy the angle at P. Why it matters: the parallel construction is an angle copy. Evidence: describes and justifies the angle copy.

branches.skill: Converse: congruent corresponding angles give parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify that the result is parallel. Why it matters: the construction relies on the converse. Evidence: applies the converses.

branches.skill: Recognize parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot recognize the goal. Why it matters: the result must never meet ℓ. Evidence: identifies parallel lines.

branches.skill: Justify the parallel-line constructions
branches.new_demand: Prove that each parallel construction is correct.

branches.skill: Divide a segment into equal parts with parallel lines
branches.new_demand: Use the parallel construction to partition a segment, justified by proportionality.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: repeated justified parallels divide a segment into equal parts.

sets.target_skill: Construct an equilateral triangle inscribed in a given circle

branches.skill: Central angles of a regular polygon
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the 120° spacing. Why it matters: the triangle's vertices are equally spaced on the circle. Evidence: uses central angles.

branches.skill: Copy a length with a compass
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot step lengths around the circle. Why it matters: the construction transfers the radius. Evidence: uses a fixed compass opening.

branches.skill: Circle vocabulary: center, radius, chord, diameter
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what "inscribed" requires. Why it matters: every vertex must be on the circle. Evidence: uses circle vocabulary.

branches.skill: Justify that the inscribed triangle is equilateral
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction produces an equilateral triangle, using circle relationships.

branches.skill: Construct a regular dodecagon by bisecting arcs
branches.new_demand: Extend the construction to a new regular polygon by bisecting arcs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: knowing why the 60° steps work, halve them to get more vertices.

sets.target_skill: Construct a square inscribed in a given circle

branches.skill: Construct a perpendicular bisector
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot create the second diameter. Why it matters: the square comes from two perpendicular diameters. Evidence: uses the perpendicular bisector construction.

branches.skill: Diagonals of a square
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why the result is a square. Why it matters: its diagonals are the two diameters. Evidence: states the diagonal properties.

branches.skill: Diameters and the center of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use diameters. Why it matters: the square's diagonals are diameters. Evidence: uses diameter facts.

branches.skill: Justify that the inscribed quadrilateral is a square
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction yields a square, and use the proof to compute.

branches.skill: Construct a regular octagon inscribed in a circle
branches.new_demand: Extend the square construction to a regular octagon by bisecting.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: halving the justified 90° central angles gives eight equal arcs.

sets.target_skill: Construct a regular hexagon inscribed in a given circle

branches.skill: Construct an inscribed equilateral triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect the two constructions. Why it matters: the hexagon uses the same six points. Evidence: relates the two constructions.

branches.skill: An equilateral triangle has equal sides and 60° angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the six equilateral triangles. Why it matters: they explain why the radius steps around exactly six times. Evidence: uses equilateral triangle facts.

branches.skill: Circle facts: radius and chord
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot relate the chord to the radius. Why it matters: each hexagon side equals the radius. Evidence: uses radius and chord facts.

branches.skill: Justify that the inscribed hexagon is regular
branches.new_demand: Prove that the construction yields a regular hexagon.

branches.skill: Use inscribed hexagons to estimate π
branches.new_demand: Use the construction in an informal limit argument for the circumference (estimating π).
branches.builds_on: A second, separate extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 proves the hexagon is regular; FORWARD 2 uses it to bound π.

sets.target_skill: Verify with coordinates that a dilation maps a line not through its center to a parallel line and leaves a line through the center unchanged

branches.skill: Dilate points with coordinates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot dilate a point. Why it matters: checking a line's image starts with images of its points. Evidence: applies (x, y) → (kx, ky).

branches.skill: Compare slopes to test whether lines are parallel
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot decide whether two lines are parallel. Why it matters: the property is about parallel images. Evidence: compares slopes.

branches.skill: Write the equation of a line through two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name the image line. Why it matters: the image line is described by an equation. Evidence: writes line equations from two points.

branches.skill: Dilate lines about a center other than the origin
branches.new_demand: Carry out the verification when the center is not the origin.

branches.skill: Prove algebraically that a dilation maps a line to a parallel line
branches.new_demand: Generalize the verification with parameters into a proof for every line.
branches.builds_on: FORWARD 1 verifies for any center; FORWARD 2 proves the property for every line algebraically.

sets.target_skill: Verify with coordinates and measurements that a dilated segment is k times as long as the original

branches.skill: Find lengths with the distance formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute lengths. Why it matters: the property compares lengths. Evidence: uses the distance formula.

branches.skill: Scale factor in scale drawings
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student treats a scale factor as something added. Why it matters: dilation multiplies lengths. Evidence: applies scale factors.

branches.skill: Dilate points about the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the dilated endpoints. Why it matters: lengths are computed from images. Evidence: dilates points.

branches.skill: Find the center or scale factor from a segment and its image
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the scale factor and center from a segment and its image.

branches.skill: Perimeter and area of dilated figures
branches.new_demand: Extend from one length to whole-figure measures: perimeter scales by k and area by k².
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 reverses the length relationship; FORWARD 2 applies it to perimeter and area.

sets.target_skill: Given two figures, decide whether they are similar by finding a similarity transformation (dilation and rigid motions) or explaining why none exists

branches.skill: Similar figures as a sequence of transformations including a dilation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect similarity with transformations. Why it matters: the decision is made with a similarity transformation. Evidence: describes similarity sequences.

branches.skill: Specify a sequence of rigid motions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish the sequence after scaling. Why it matters: a similarity sequence ends with rigid motions. Evidence: names rigid motions from rules.

branches.skill: Dilate figures about the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot apply the scaling step. Why it matters: similarity sequences include a dilation. Evidence: dilates figures.

branches.skill: Find the scale factor and correspondence when the image is turned or flipped
branches.new_demand: Decide similarity and its correspondence when the figures are in different orientations, using side ratios.

branches.skill: Prove that all circles are similar
branches.new_demand: Extend the transformation definition of similarity to curved figures (circles).
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 handles turned and flipped triangles; FORWARD 2 applies the definition to circles.

sets.target_skill: Explain, using similarity transformations, why similar triangles have all corresponding angles congruent and all corresponding sides proportional, and use this meaning

branches.skill: Read correspondence from a similarity or congruence statement
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student mismatches parts. Why it matters: proportional sides must be corresponding sides. Evidence: reads correspondences.

branches.skill: Solve proportions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot solve proportions. Why it matters: missing sides are found with proportions. Evidence: solves and checks proportions.

branches.skill: Scale factor between figures
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use one factor for all sides. Why it matters: the meaning of similarity is one common ratio. Evidence: finds and applies scale factors.

branches.skill: Use the AA criterion to recognize similar triangles
branches.new_demand: Move from the full definition (all angles and sides) to a shortcut criterion (AA).

branches.skill: Use similarity to find unknown lengths in problems
branches.new_demand: Apply the meaning of similarity to solve real and geometric problems.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: once AA identifies similar triangles, their proportional sides solve problems.

sets.target_skill: Use the properties of similarity transformations to prove that two triangles with two pairs of congruent angles are similar

branches.skill: Prove triangles congruent with ASA
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish with a congruence. Why it matters: the AA proof ends with ASA. Evidence: applies ASA.

branches.skill: Dilations multiply lengths and keep angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what the dilation step does. Why it matters: the proof relies on matching one side and keeping angles. Evidence: states dilation properties.

branches.skill: Use the angle sum to find a third angle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why two angles suffice. Why it matters: the third angle follows from the sum. Evidence: computes third angles.

branches.skill: Establish the SAS and SSS similarity criteria
branches.new_demand: Extend the transformation proof to the other similarity criteria (SAS and SSS).

branches.skill: Use AA to set up and solve problems
branches.new_demand: Use AA to identify similar triangles in problems and solve for lengths.
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 proves more criteria; FORWARD 2 uses AA as a tool in applied problems.

sets.target_skill: Prove that a line parallel to one side of a triangle divides the other two sides proportionally

branches.skill: Use AA to show triangles are similar
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the similarity. Why it matters: the theorem is proved from △ADE ~ △ABC. Evidence: uses AA and its ratios.

branches.skill: Corresponding angles of parallel lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify the congruent angles. Why it matters: they come from DE ∥ BC. Evidence: names corresponding angles.

branches.skill: Rewrite and solve proportions algebraically
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot convert the similarity proportion. Why it matters: the theorem's proportion is a rewritten form. Evidence: manipulates proportions.

branches.skill: Prove that parallel lines cut transversals proportionally
branches.new_demand: Generalize the theorem to three parallel lines cutting any two transversals.

branches.skill: Prove the angle bisector theorem
branches.new_demand: Use the triangle proportionality theorem as a tool to prove a new relationship (the angle bisector theorem).
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 generalizes the theorem; FORWARD 2 uses it to prove another theorem.

sets.target_skill: Prove that a line dividing two sides of a triangle proportionally is parallel to the third side

branches.skill: Use the triangle proportionality theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the forward theorem. Why it matters: the converse reverses it. Evidence: applies and states the theorem.

branches.skill: SAS similarity
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the similarity from ratios. Why it matters: the converse proof uses SAS similarity. Evidence: applies SAS similarity.

branches.skill: Converse of the corresponding angles theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot conclude parallel lines. Why it matters: the last step of the proof. Evidence: applies the converse.

branches.skill: Use the converse to decide parallelism in figures
branches.new_demand: Use the converse to find unknown lengths that force parallelism, and connect it to the midsegment theorem.

branches.skill: Prove the trapezoid midsegment theorem
branches.new_demand: Combine the converse with midsegments to prove a new theorem about trapezoids.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the parallel conditions found there combine into the trapezoid midsegment proof.

sets.target_skill: Prove the Pythagorean Theorem using triangle similarity (the altitude to the hypotenuse)

branches.skill: Show triangles similar with AA
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot see the three similar triangles. Why it matters: the proof is built on them. Evidence: identifies AA in the altitude figure.

branches.skill: Cross-multiply proportions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot turn proportions into products. Why it matters: the proof uses b² = c · AD. Evidence: cross-multiplies.

branches.skill: Explain a proof of the Pythagorean Theorem informally
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what is being proved. Why it matters: the proof must establish this statement in general. Evidence: states and applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Use the geometric mean relationships in a right triangle
branches.new_demand: Derive and use further relationships (geometric means) from the same similar triangles.

branches.skill: The Law of Cosines as a generalization of the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.new_demand: See the theorem as the C = 90° case of a general relationship, and classify triangles by comparing squares.
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 extracts more right-triangle relationships; FORWARD 2 generalizes to all triangles (advanced strand).

sets.target_skill: Identify similar triangles with a criterion and use them to find unknown lengths in figures and situations

branches.skill: Similarity criteria: AA, SAS, SSS
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify the similarity. Why it matters: each problem starts by naming a criterion. Evidence: names criteria.

branches.skill: Solve proportions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish the computation. Why it matters: unknown lengths come from proportions. Evidence: solves proportions.

branches.skill: Identify corresponding sides in overlapping triangles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student pairs a piece of a side with a whole side. Why it matters: proportions must use corresponding whole sides. Evidence: matches corresponding sides.

branches.skill: Solve multistep problems with two or more pairs of similar triangles
branches.new_demand: Solve problems that need two linked similarities or a hidden pair of similar triangles.

branches.skill: Solve similarity problems with algebra (unknowns on both sides)
branches.new_demand: Set up and solve similarity problems whose unknowns lead to quadratic equations (rejecting invalid roots).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the same linked similarities, now with algebraic unknowns.

sets.target_skill: Prove a relationship in a geometric figure by first proving two triangles congruent with a criterion

branches.skill: Choose and apply SSS, SAS, ASA, AAS
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot pick a criterion. Why it matters: every proof starts with a congruence. Evidence: chooses criteria.

branches.skill: Find hidden parts: shared sides, vertical angles, right angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses parts not stated in the problem. Why it matters: proofs depend on them. Evidence: finds hidden congruent parts.

branches.skill: Use corresponding parts to finish a proof
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student stops after the congruence. Why it matters: the goal is a relationship about specific parts. Evidence: states the final conclusion.

branches.skill: Prove relationships that need two congruences in a row
branches.new_demand: Prove relationships that need a chain of two congruences.

branches.skill: Decide which given data are sufficient for a proof, and supply a missing condition
branches.new_demand: Judge sufficiency of data and identify a missing condition, with justification.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: before chaining congruences, decide whether each step has enough data.

sets.target_skill: Prove a relationship (such as a product or proportion of lengths) by first proving two triangles similar

branches.skill: Prove triangles similar with AA
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot establish the similarity. Why it matters: each proof starts with AA. Evidence: applies AA.

branches.skill: Turn a proportion into a product
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rewrite the proportion. Why it matters: the result is a product. Evidence: cross-multiplies.

branches.skill: Match corresponding sides of similar triangles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student pairs the wrong sides. Why it matters: the product must use corresponding sides. Evidence: writes correct proportions.

branches.skill: Use proved product relationships to compute
branches.new_demand: Apply the proved relationships as tools to compute unknown lengths.

branches.skill: Prove relationships in circles with similar triangles
branches.new_demand: Use similarity proofs in circle configurations (tangents and secants).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the chord product extends to tangents and secants.

sets.target_skill: Explain why right-triangle side ratios depend only on the acute angle (by similarity) and define sine, cosine, and tangent from them

branches.skill: Similar triangles have equal side ratios within each triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see ratios inside a triangle as fixed by shape. Why it matters: trig ratios are such ratios. Evidence: compares internal ratios.

branches.skill: Name the opposite side, adjacent side, and hypotenuse for an angle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student labels sides relative to the wrong angle. Why it matters: every ratio is defined relative to the chosen angle. Evidence: labels sides.

branches.skill: Write and simplify ratios
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot work with ratios. Why it matters: trig values are ratios. Evidence: writes and simplifies ratios.

branches.skill: Find trig ratios from one ratio, using a similar right triangle
branches.new_demand: Work backward from one ratio to the others by building a similar right triangle.

branches.skill: The unit circle extends the ratios beyond acute angles
branches.new_demand: Extend the ratio definitions to all angles using the unit circle (Algebra II).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the triangle with hypotenuse 1 is the step to the unit circle.

sets.target_skill: Explain why sin θ = cos(90° - θ) and use the relationship to rewrite and solve

branches.skill: Complementary angles add to 90°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know "complementary". Why it matters: the relationship is about complementary angles. Evidence: finds complements.

branches.skill: Opposite and adjacent sides depend on the chosen angle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student labels sides only for one angle. Why it matters: the relationship swaps the roles of the two acute angles. Evidence: labels sides for each angle.

branches.skill: Angle sum in a right triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the two acute angles as complementary. Why it matters: that is why the relationship holds. Evidence: uses the right-triangle angle sum.

branches.skill: Relationships between tangents of complementary angles
branches.new_demand: Extend the complementary relationship to tangent (reciprocals) and to new identities.

branches.skill: The Pythagorean identity
branches.new_demand: Prove and use the Pythagorean identity, which Algebra II extends to all angles.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: combining complementary relationships with the Pythagorean Theorem gives the identity.

sets.target_skill: Use sine, cosine, or tangent to find an unknown side of a right triangle in an applied problem

branches.skill: Choose the trigonometric ratio that links the known and unknown sides
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student picks the wrong ratio. Why it matters: the ratio must contain the known and the unknown side. Evidence: chooses sine, cosine, or tangent.

branches.skill: Solve one-variable equations with a multiplication or division
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot solve the trig equation for the side. Why it matters: the unknown may be in the numerator or the denominator. Evidence: solves both forms.

branches.skill: Round to a stated precision and keep track of units
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student rounds early or drops units. Why it matters: applied answers need the stated precision and units. Evidence: rounds correctly and labels units.

branches.skill: Find a height from two angle-of-elevation observations
branches.new_demand: Solve an inverse problem with two observations: two trigonometric equations in two unknowns.

branches.skill: Find a feasible location under a clearance constraint
branches.new_demand: Design under a constraint: find the extreme feasible dimension and decide which way to round.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the same trigonometric models, now used to satisfy a stated constraint.

sets.target_skill: Use inverse sine, cosine, or tangent to find an acute angle of a right triangle in an applied problem

branches.skill: Inverse trig undoes a trig ratio
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know how to get an angle from a ratio. Why it matters: every angle problem ends with an inverse ratio. Evidence: uses inverse trig.

branches.skill: Choose the ratio from the two known sides
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the wrong ratio. Why it matters: the inverse must match the known sides. Evidence: chooses the ratio.

branches.skill: Use degree mode and round angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student gets impossible angles from mode or rounding errors. Why it matters: answers must be reasonable acute angles. Evidence: checks mode and rounding.

branches.skill: Solve a right triangle completely from two sides
branches.new_demand: Find ALL missing parts of a right triangle and check them for consistency.

branches.skill: Find directions (bearings) with inverse trigonometry
branches.new_demand: Model navigation situations as right triangles and report directions as angles.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving the whole triangle gives both distance and direction.

sets.target_skill: Find all requested parts of a right triangle in an applied problem, choosing trigonometric ratios and the Pythagorean Theorem

branches.skill: Use the Pythagorean Theorem to find a side
