branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find a side without trig. Why it matters: often the quickest step uses the Pythagorean Theorem. Evidence: applies it in both directions.

branches.skill: Interpret angles of elevation and depression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student puts the angle in the wrong place. Why it matters: the triangle must be set up correctly before solving. Evidence: locates elevation and depression angles.

branches.skill: Choose sine, cosine, or tangent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot plan which ratio to use. Why it matters: each requested part needs its own ratio. Evidence: chooses ratios.

branches.skill: Solve problems that need two right triangles
branches.new_demand: Combine two right triangles that share a side to answer a question neither triangle answers alone.

branches.skill: Solve non-right triangles with the Law of Sines
branches.new_demand: Extend from right triangles to oblique triangles with the Law of Sines (advanced strand).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: two right triangles sharing an altitude are exactly how the Law of Sines is derived.

sets.target_skill: Prove that any two circles are similar by giving a similarity transformation that maps one onto the other

branches.skill: A dilation multiplies distances by the scale factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what a dilation does to distances. Why it matters: the proof scales the radius. Evidence: applies scale factors to radii.

branches.skill: Translate a point to another point
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot move one center onto the other. Why it matters: the proof starts with a translation. Evidence: finds translations.

branches.skill: A circle is all points at one distance from its center
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the definition. Why it matters: the proof checks distances from the center. Evidence: uses the definition.

branches.skill: Find a single dilation that maps one circle onto another
branches.new_demand: Find the single dilation (center and factor) relating two circles, an inverse problem.

branches.skill: Arcs of similar circles scale with the radius
branches.new_demand: Use the similarity of circles to compare arcs (the start of radian measure).
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 finds the dilation; FORWARD 2 uses the similarity to scale arc lengths.

sets.target_skill: Identify and describe the relationship between a central angle and an inscribed angle that intercept the same arc

branches.skill: Base angles of an isosceles triangle are congruent
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses the isosceles triangle formed by two radii. Why it matters: the proof uses its base angles. Evidence: uses isosceles base angles.

branches.skill: The exterior angle theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the doubling. Why it matters: the central angle is an exterior angle of the isosceles triangle. Evidence: applies the exterior angle theorem.

branches.skill: A central angle and its arc have the same measure
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect central angles with arcs. Why it matters: the relationship is stated with arcs. Evidence: converts between arcs and central angles.

branches.skill: Prove the inscribed angle theorem when the center is inside or outside the angle
branches.new_demand: Complete the proof for every position of the center (all three cases).

branches.skill: Inscribed angles on the same arc, and arc applications
branches.new_demand: Derive consequences of the theorem (congruent inscribed angles, angles between chords) and use them.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: with the theorem proved in all cases, its consequences follow.

sets.target_skill: Explain why an angle inscribed in a semicircle (on a diameter) is a right angle, and use it

branches.skill: Use the inscribed angle theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the inscribed angle theorem. Why it matters: the result is the case of a 180° arc. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Isosceles triangles from radii
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses the isosceles triangles. Why it matters: the alternative proof uses them. Evidence: uses equal radii.

branches.skill: Triangle angle sum
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot finish the angle argument. Why it matters: the proof ends with the angle sum. Evidence: uses the angle sum.

branches.skill: Use the converse to find a circle through a right triangle
branches.new_demand: Prove and use the converse: a right angle's hypotenuse is a diameter.

branches.skill: Use the diameter property to construct tangents from an external point
branches.new_demand: Use the property to construct tangents from an external point (advanced strand).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the circle on a diameter locates the right-angle points needed for tangents.

sets.target_skill: Explain why a tangent line is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency, and use it

branches.skill: Use the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute with the right triangle formed by the radius and tangent. Why it matters: tangent problems are right-triangle problems. Evidence: uses the theorem and converse.

branches.skill: The perpendicular is the shortest segment from a point to a line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the shortest-distance fact. Why it matters: the indirect proof relies on it. Evidence: explains shortest distance.

branches.skill: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is unclear what tangent means. Why it matters: the proof uses the one-point property. Evidence: uses the definition.

branches.skill: Tangent segments from an external point are congruent
branches.new_demand: Prove and use a new consequence: tangent segments from one point are congruent.

branches.skill: Write the equation of a tangent line in the coordinate plane
branches.new_demand: Use radius ⊥ tangent with slopes to write tangent line equations.
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 stays synthetic; FORWARD 2 moves the same fact to coordinates.

sets.target_skill: Describe and use the relationship between a circumscribed angle and the central angle that intercepts the same arc (they are supplementary)

branches.skill: A tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of tangency
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not use the right angles. Why it matters: they are the key to the relationship. Evidence: uses radius ⊥ tangent.

branches.skill: The angles of a quadrilateral add to 360°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the quadrilateral angle sum. Why it matters: the proof uses it. Evidence: applies 360°.

branches.skill: Supplementary angles add to 180°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know "supplementary". Why it matters: the relationship is supplementary angles. Evidence: finds supplements.

branches.skill: Use the circumscribed angle with arcs, including major arcs
branches.new_demand: Express the circumscribed angle in terms of both arcs and combine it with inscribed angles.

branches.skill: Angles formed by secants and tangents outside a circle
branches.new_demand: Generalize to angles formed outside the circle by secants (proof and use).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the "half the difference of the arcs" form found there extends to secants.

sets.target_skill: Identify and use relationships among radii and chords: a radius perpendicular to a chord bisects it, and congruent chords are equidistant from the center

branches.skill: Right triangles: Hypotenuse-Leg and the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot prove the two halves equal. Why it matters: the proof uses the two right triangles. Evidence: uses HL and the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: The perpendicular bisector theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect chords to perpendicular bisectors. Why it matters: the center is on every chord's bisector. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Radii of a circle are equal
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the equal radii. Why it matters: they make the isosceles triangle. Evidence: uses equal radii.

branches.skill: Locate the center of a circle from chords
branches.new_demand: Use the chord relationships in reverse to locate a circle's center (inverse problem).

branches.skill: Find chord lengths and central angles with trigonometry
branches.new_demand: Combine the perpendicular-bisector relationship with trigonometry to relate chords and central angles.
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 finds centers; FORWARD 2 measures chords with trigonometry.

sets.target_skill: Construct the inscribed circle (incircle) of a given triangle with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Construct an angle bisector
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot bisect the angles. Why it matters: the incenter is found with two angle bisectors. Evidence: bisects angles.

branches.skill: Construct a perpendicular from a point to a line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the wrong radius. Why it matters: the radius is the perpendicular distance to a side. Evidence: constructs perpendiculars.

branches.skill: Points on an angle bisector are equidistant from the sides
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why the incenter works. Why it matters: equal distances to the sides make one circle touch all three. Evidence: uses the bisector distance property.

branches.skill: Prove that the incenter is equidistant from the sides
branches.new_demand: Prove why the construction works and derive the inradius formula.

branches.skill: Locate a point equidistant from three lines in a design
branches.new_demand: Use the incircle to solve a design problem with a constraint (largest circle touching three lines).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the inradius formula finds the largest feasible circle in a design.

sets.target_skill: Construct the circumscribed circle (circumcircle) of a given triangle with compass and straightedge

branches.skill: Construct the perpendicular bisector of a segment
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot construct the bisectors. Why it matters: they locate the center. Evidence: constructs perpendicular bisectors.

branches.skill: Points on the perpendicular bisector are equidistant from the endpoints
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know why the bisectors locate the center. Why it matters: equidistance from vertices is needed. Evidence: uses the theorem.

branches.skill: Triangle types: acute, right, obtuse
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student is surprised when the center is outside. Why it matters: the type of triangle decides where the center is. Evidence: classifies triangles.

branches.skill: Find the circumcenter and radius with coordinates
branches.new_demand: Locate the circumcenter algebraically with perpendicular bisector equations.

branches.skill: Find the circumradius with trigonometry (extended Law of Sines)
branches.new_demand: Connect the circumcircle with trigonometry (the extended Law of Sines, advanced strand).
branches.builds_on: A second extension of MAIN: FORWARD 1 computes the center; FORWARD 2 computes the radius from an angle.

sets.target_skill: Prove that the opposite angles of a quadrilateral inscribed in a circle are supplementary, and use the property

branches.skill: The inscribed angle theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot relate the angles to arcs. Why it matters: the proof uses the inscribed angle theorem twice. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Supplementary angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know supplementary. Why it matters: the theorem states supplementary angles. Evidence: finds supplements.

branches.skill: Arcs of a circle add to 360°
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the two arcs fill the circle. Why it matters: that gives the 180° sum. Evidence: adds arcs.

branches.skill: Use the converse: decide whether a quadrilateral can be inscribed
branches.new_demand: Use the property and its converse to decide whether a quadrilateral is cyclic and to solve for unknowns.

branches.skill: Exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral
branches.new_demand: Derive and use a further consequence (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: supplementary opposite angles combined with linear pairs.

sets.target_skill: Use similarity to show that the arc cut off by an angle is proportional to the radius, define radian measure as the constant of proportionality, and use s = rθ

branches.skill: Similar figures: lengths scale by the scale factor
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not apply similarity to arcs. Why it matters: the derivation is a similarity argument. Evidence: scales arcs.

branches.skill: Circumference of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the whole circumference. Why it matters: an arc is a fraction of it. Evidence: uses C = 2πr.

branches.skill: Find a fraction of a whole
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the fraction of the circle. Why it matters: arc length = fraction × circumference. Evidence: computes fractions of a circle.

branches.skill: Convert between degrees and radians
branches.new_demand: Work fluently between degree and radian measure, using the definition s = rθ.

branches.skill: Radian measure for angles of rotation and the unit circle
branches.new_demand: Use radians for angles of rotation, including angles beyond 2π (Algebra II).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: radian fluency extends to rotation angles on the unit circle.

sets.target_skill: Derive the area of a sector as a fraction of the circle's area (in degrees and radians) and use it

branches.skill: Area of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the whole-circle area (or uses the diameter). Why it matters: a sector is a fraction of it. Evidence: uses A = πr² with the radius.

branches.skill: The radius is half the diameter
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student plugs in the diameter. Why it matters: sector formulas need the radius. Evidence: converts diameter to radius.

branches.skill: Fractions of a circle in degrees and radians
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find what fraction of the circle a sector is. Why it matters: the derivation multiplies the area by that fraction. Evidence: finds fractions in both units.

branches.skill: Solve inverse sector problems
branches.new_demand: Solve the inverse problem: find the radius or angle from a sector area.

branches.skill: Areas of segments and composite circular regions
branches.new_demand: Model regions made of sectors, triangles, and rings, and compute their areas.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: sector areas combine with other figures in modeling problems.

sets.target_skill: Derive the equation of a circle with given center and radius using the Pythagorean Theorem, and write the equation of a circle from given information

branches.skill: Distance between two points with the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find distances on the plane. Why it matters: the radius is the distance from the center to a point. Evidence: finds distances with the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Use the Pythagorean Theorem with expressions
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the Pythagorean relationship with variable legs. Why it matters: the derivation uses legs x - h and y - k. Evidence: writes the theorem with expressions.

branches.skill: Shifting a graph: reading h and k
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reverses the signs of the center. Why it matters: the center (h, k) appears as x - h and y - k. Evidence: reads shifts correctly.

branches.skill: Write circle equations from other given information
branches.new_demand: Use the derived equation when the radius or center must first be found (diameter endpoints, tangency).

branches.skill: Prove or disprove that points lie on a circle
branches.new_demand: Use the circle equation as a test in a coordinate proof.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: circles found from diameters and tangency are tested against given points.

sets.target_skill: Complete the square to find the center and radius of a circle given by an equation in general form

branches.skill: Complete the square in one variable
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot complete the square. Why it matters: it is the main step. Evidence: completes squares in one variable.

branches.skill: Square a binomial
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why the added number makes a square. Why it matters: checking the completed square needs expansion. Evidence: expands binomial squares.

branches.skill: Keep an equation balanced
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student adds to one side only and gets the wrong radius. Why it matters: r² comes from the balanced right side. Evidence: keeps equations balanced.

branches.skill: Leading coefficients and equations that are not circles
branches.new_demand: Handle leading coefficients and decide when an equation is not a circle.

branches.skill: Complete the square for an ellipse
branches.new_demand: Use completing the square on a conic whose squared terms have different coefficients (advanced strand).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: factoring out leading coefficients is the key step for ellipses.

sets.target_skill: Derive the equation of a parabola given its focus and directrix

branches.skill: Distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the distance to the focus. Why it matters: one side of the defining equation is that distance. Evidence: writes the distance expression.

branches.skill: Distance from a point to a horizontal line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the distance to the directrix. Why it matters: the other side of the defining equation is that distance. Evidence: finds vertical distances.

branches.skill: Points equidistant from two objects
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the definition. Why it matters: the equation encodes equal distances. Evidence: states and uses the definition.

branches.skill: Expand and simplify squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot simplify after squaring. Why it matters: the y² terms must cancel. Evidence: expands and simplifies.

branches.skill: Find the focus and directrix from an equation
branches.new_demand: Reverse the derivation: read the focus and directrix from an equation.

branches.skill: Design with the reflective property of parabolas
branches.new_demand: Apply the focus to a design problem (placing a receiver or bulb).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reading the focus from an equation locates the receiver.

sets.target_skill: Use slopes and distances to prove or disprove that a quadrilateral or triangle defined by coordinates has a given type

branches.skill: Find the slope between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find slopes. Why it matters: parallel and perpendicular sides are decided by slopes. Evidence: computes slopes.

branches.skill: Find the distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compare side lengths. Why it matters: rhombus and square proofs compare lengths. Evidence: computes distances.

branches.skill: Properties that define special quadrilaterals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know what must be shown. Why it matters: the proof checks the defining property. Evidence: states the needed properties.

branches.skill: Coordinate proofs with variables
branches.new_demand: Prove general theorems with variable coordinates instead of checking one example.

branches.skill: Use the classification to find area
branches.new_demand: Use the proved type to choose and apply an area formula.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: after proving the type (with numbers or variables), its properties give the area.

sets.target_skill: Use coordinates to prove or disprove statements about points on circles and equal distances

branches.skill: Distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the distance to the center. Why it matters: it decides whether the point is on the circle. Evidence: computes distances.

branches.skill: The equation of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read the center and radius. Why it matters: the proof compares with r. Evidence: reads circle equations.

branches.skill: Substitute values into an expression
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes sign errors substituting. Why it matters: checks are substitutions. Evidence: evaluates correctly.

branches.skill: Coordinate proofs about circles with variables
branches.new_demand: Prove circle statements for every point using variables (Thales' theorem by slopes).

branches.skill: Find the tangent line to a circle at a point
branches.new_demand: Combine the circle equation with the perpendicular slope criterion to write tangent lines.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the slope products used there now give tangent lines.

sets.target_skill: Prove that nonvertical lines are parallel exactly when their slopes are equal, and perpendicular exactly when the product of their slopes is -1

branches.skill: Similar slope triangles give the same slope
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why one line has one slope. Why it matters: the proof uses slope triangles. Evidence: explains constant slope.

branches.skill: Rotate a point 90° about the origin
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rotate points. Why it matters: the perpendicular proof rotates (a, b). Evidence: rotates points 90°.

branches.skill: Negative reciprocals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot simplify the product. Why it matters: the proof ends with (b/a)(-a/b) = -1. Evidence: computes negative reciprocals.

branches.skill: Use the criteria to classify pairs of lines
branches.new_demand: Apply the proved criteria to lines in different forms, including the vertical/horizontal exception.

branches.skill: Use the criteria inside a general coordinate proof
branches.new_demand: Use the slope criteria as a tool in general coordinate proofs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: classifying lines by slope becomes a step in proving theorems.

sets.target_skill: Use the slope criteria to write the equation of a line parallel or perpendicular to a given line through a given point

branches.skill: Read the slope of a line
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read the given line's slope. Why it matters: the new slope comes from it. Evidence: reads slopes from equations.

branches.skill: Rewrite an equation in slope-intercept form
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student reads the slope from standard form incorrectly. Why it matters: many given lines are in standard form. Evidence: solves for y.

branches.skill: Write a line from a point and a slope
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write a line from a point and slope. Why it matters: that is the last step. Evidence: writes linear equations.

branches.skill: Opposite reciprocals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the opposite or the reciprocal only. Why it matters: perpendicular slopes need both. Evidence: finds negative reciprocals.

branches.skill: Write perpendicular bisectors and altitudes
branches.new_demand: Combine the midpoint or a vertex with a perpendicular slope to write special lines of triangles.

branches.skill: Find the distance from a point to a line
branches.new_demand: Use a perpendicular line to compute a point-to-line distance.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: writing perpendicular lines through a point is the first step.

sets.target_skill: Use the slope criteria for parallel and perpendicular lines to solve geometric problems (missing coordinates, altitudes, right angles)

branches.skill: Slope from two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find slopes. Why it matters: every problem compares slopes. Evidence: computes slopes.

branches.skill: Solve a linear equation for an unknown
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student sets up the slope condition but cannot solve it. Why it matters: unknown coordinates come from equations. Evidence: solves linear equations.

branches.skill: Equations of parallel and perpendicular lines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the needed perpendicular line. Why it matters: the altitude foot needs it. Evidence: writes parallel and perpendicular lines.

branches.skill: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find a missing vertex. Why it matters: parallel opposite sides locate it. Evidence: uses parallelogram properties.

branches.skill: Find the orthocenter of a triangle
branches.new_demand: Solve a multi-step problem that combines two perpendicular lines into a system.

branches.skill: Shortest path to a straight line in a design
branches.new_demand: Use the perpendicular-foot computation to minimize a length in a design problem.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: intersecting a line with a perpendicular through a point.

sets.target_skill: Find the point on a directed line segment between two given points that partitions the segment in a given ratio

branches.skill: A ratio as a fraction of the whole
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses 1/2 for 1 : 2. Why it matters: the fraction is part over total parts. Evidence: converts ratios to fractions of the whole.

branches.skill: Horizontal and vertical change
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the run and rise of the segment. Why it matters: the partition takes a fraction of each. Evidence: finds signed changes.

branches.skill: Find a fraction of a number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot take the fraction of the change. Why it matters: P = start + fraction × change. Evidence: computes fractions of signed numbers.

branches.skill: Work backward: find an endpoint or the ratio
branches.new_demand: Reverse the partition: find an endpoint or the ratio from known points.

branches.skill: The centroid as a partition point
branches.new_demand: Use partitioning in a general coordinate proof (the centroid formula).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reasoning about partition ratios with unknown points becomes a general proof.

sets.target_skill: Use coordinates and the distance formula to compute perimeters of polygons

branches.skill: Distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find slanted side lengths. Why it matters: most sides are slanted. Evidence: uses the distance formula.

branches.skill: Lengths of horizontal and vertical sides
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student overcomplicates horizontal and vertical sides. Why it matters: they are counted directly. Evidence: finds horizontal and vertical lengths.

branches.skill: Simplify square roots
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot combine radical side lengths. Why it matters: exact perimeters need it. Evidence: simplifies and adds radicals.

branches.skill: Find a missing coordinate from a perimeter
branches.new_demand: Use the perimeter relationship as an equation to find unknown coordinates.

branches.skill: Fencing and cost from a coordinate plan
branches.new_demand: Use perimeters from coordinates with scales and unit costs in a design problem.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: perimeters computed from coordinates now carry units and cost.

sets.target_skill: Use coordinates to compute areas of triangles and rectangles (by base and height, side lengths, or a bounding rectangle)

branches.skill: Area of a triangle from base and height
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the triangle area formula. Why it matters: every method uses it. Evidence: computes triangle areas.

branches.skill: Lengths on the coordinate plane
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot read bases and heights from coordinates. Why it matters: they come from coordinates. Evidence: finds lengths on the grid.

branches.skill: Distance between two points
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find slanted side lengths. Why it matters: tilted rectangles need them. Evidence: computes distances.

branches.skill: Find a missing vertex from an area
branches.new_demand: Use the area relationship as an equation to find unknown coordinates.

branches.skill: Use area from coordinates with density
branches.new_demand: Use areas computed from coordinates in density models.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: area from coordinates is now a step in a modeling computation.

sets.target_skill: Give informal arguments (similarity, rolling, and limits of polygon perimeters) for the formula C = πd = 2πr for the circumference of a circle

branches.skill: Circumference formulas
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the formula being justified. Why it matters: the argument explains it. Evidence: states and uses the circumference formula.

branches.skill: Perimeters of regular polygons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find polygon perimeters. Why it matters: the polygon argument compares them with the circumference. Evidence: computes perimeters of regular polygons.

branches.skill: All circles are similar
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why π is a constant. Why it matters: the circumference argument uses similarity. Evidence: uses similarity of circles.

branches.skill: Trap π between inscribed and circumscribed polygons
branches.new_demand: Bound the circumference from both sides and turn the bounds into an estimate of π.

branches.skill: Extend the circumference argument to arcs and curved boundaries
branches.new_demand: Extend the circumference argument from whole circles to arcs and boundaries made of arcs and segments.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: polygon bounds for the whole circle become chord approximations and proportional arcs.

sets.target_skill: Give informal arguments (dissection into sectors or rings, similarity, and estimation) for the formula A = πr² for the area of a circle

branches.skill: Area of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the formula being justified. Why it matters: the argument explains it. Evidence: states and uses the area formula.

branches.skill: Area of a parallelogram
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the area of the rearranged shape. Why it matters: the argument ends with base × height. Evidence: finds parallelogram areas.

branches.skill: Scale factors and area
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know how area scales. Why it matters: the similarity argument uses k². Evidence: scales areas.

branches.skill: Area of a circle as a limit of regular polygons
branches.new_demand: Give a second, polygon-limit argument and connect perimeter and area formulas.

branches.skill: From area to volume: stacking disks
branches.new_demand: Use the circle area as the base of a volume argument (the next part of the same standard).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: once the circle's area is justified, it becomes the base area in the cylinder argument.

sets.target_skill: Give an informal argument (stacking congruent cross-sections and Cavalieri's principle) for the formula V = πr²h for the volume of a cylinder

branches.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism as layers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see volume as stacked layers. Why it matters: the cylinder argument extends it. Evidence: computes prism volume as layers.

branches.skill: Area of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the base area. Why it matters: V = (base area) × h. Evidence: finds circle areas.

branches.skill: Cross-sections parallel to the base
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see the congruent layers. Why it matters: the argument depends on them. Evidence: describes parallel cross-sections.

branches.skill: Cavalieri's principle with different shapes
branches.new_demand: Apply Cavalieri's principle to solids with different shapes but equal cross-sectional areas.

branches.skill: Use the cylinder volume formula to solve problems
branches.new_demand: Use the justified formula in measurement problems with units and rounding.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the same base-area × height reasoning now computes real volumes.

sets.target_skill: Give informal arguments (dissection of a cube or prism, Cavalieri's principle, and stacked slabs) for V = ⅓Bh for every pyramid

branches.skill: Volume of a prism
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the prism's volume. Why it matters: the pyramid is a third of it. Evidence: computes prism volume.

branches.skill: Base area of a pyramid
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses an edge instead of the base area. Why it matters: B is an area. Evidence: finds base areas.

branches.skill: Split a volume into equal parts
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why "three equal pieces" means one third. Why it matters: the dissection argument depends on it. Evidence: splits volumes into equal parts.

branches.skill: Cavalieri's principle for pyramids
branches.new_demand: Extend the argument with Cavalieri's principle to oblique pyramids and pyramids with different base shapes.

branches.skill: Use the pyramid volume formula
branches.new_demand: Apply the justified formula to computation problems.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the ⅓Bh formula, justified for any apex position, is now applied.

sets.target_skill: Give informal arguments (limits of pyramids, Cavalieri's principle, and stacked disks) for V = ⅓πr²h for a cone

branches.skill: Area of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the base area. Why it matters: the cone formula is ⅓ × base area × height. Evidence: finds circle areas.

branches.skill: The cylinder volume argument
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compare a cone with its cylinder. Why it matters: the factor ⅓ compares them. Evidence: relates cone and cylinder volumes.

branches.skill: The pyramid volume formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the pyramid result. Why it matters: the cone argument compares the cone with pyramids. Evidence: uses V = ⅓Bh.

branches.skill: Volumes of frustums (cones with the top cut off)
branches.new_demand: Combine the cone formula with similarity to find volumes of frustums.

branches.skill: Use the cone volume formula
branches.new_demand: Apply the justified formula to computation problems with exact and rounded answers.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the cone formula, combined with similarity, now computes real volumes.

sets.target_skill: Use the volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, and cones to solve problems, giving exact values and rounded values with units

branches.skill: Area of a circle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the base area. Why it matters: every formula uses it. Evidence: finds circle areas.

branches.skill: Find a missing side with the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the slant height. Why it matters: volume uses the perpendicular height. Evidence: finds heights with the Pythagorean Theorem.

branches.skill: Evaluate a formula and round
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes arithmetic or rounding errors. Why it matters: answers need exact and rounded forms. Evidence: evaluates and rounds.

branches.skill: Which solid uses ⅓?
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student mixes the formulas. Why it matters: choosing the right formula is the first step. Evidence: matches solids and formulas.

branches.skill: Composite and hollow solids
branches.new_demand: Combine and subtract volumes for composite and hollow solids.

branches.skill: Mass from volume and density
branches.new_demand: Use the computed volume as one step in a density model.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: computed volumes (including composites) feed a density calculation.

sets.target_skill: Use V = 4/3 πr³ for spheres and hemispheres, alone and combined with cylinders and cones

branches.skill: Cubes of numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student squares or triples instead of cubing. Why it matters: the sphere formula uses r³. Evidence: computes cubes.

branches.skill: Radius from diameter
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the diameter. Why it matters: the formula needs the radius. Evidence: converts diameter to radius.

branches.skill: Multiply fractions by numbers
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes fraction errors. Why it matters: the coefficient is 4/3. Evidence: multiplies with fractions.

branches.skill: Cylinder and cone volumes
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the other parts of a composite solid. Why it matters: composites add cylinders and cones. Evidence: finds those volumes.

branches.skill: Scaling spheres
branches.new_demand: Reason about how sphere volume scales and compare it with related solids.

branches.skill: Model real objects as spheres
branches.new_demand: Choose a sphere model for a real object, compute, and judge the model.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: scale reasoning helps judge large and small real objects.

sets.target_skill: Use the volume formulas for cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres to find an unknown radius, height, or edge

branches.skill: Solve a one-step equation with a coefficient
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot isolate the unknown. Why it matters: the formula becomes an equation. Evidence: solves one-step equations.

branches.skill: Square roots and cube roots
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot undo the square or cube. Why it matters: radius problems end with a root. Evidence: takes square and cube roots.

branches.skill: Rearrange a formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rearrange a formula. Why it matters: it organizes the solution. Evidence: solves formulas for a variable.

branches.skill: Find dimensions to meet a target volume
branches.new_demand: Solve for dimensions in applied settings with rounding and comparisons between solids.

branches.skill: Design a container that meets constraints
branches.new_demand: Use the solved formulas to check a design against several constraints.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving for dimensions becomes a step in checking a design.

sets.target_skill: Identify the shapes of two-dimensional cross-sections of cylinders, cones, spheres, prisms, and pyramids for planes in different positions

branches.skill: Cross-sections of right rectangular prisms and pyramids
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot picture basic slices. Why it matters: harder solids build on them. Evidence: names cross-sections of prisms and pyramids.

branches.skill: Properties of polygons
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot name the shape found. Why it matters: answers are polygon names. Evidence: classifies polygons.

branches.skill: Parts of solids
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the parts being cut. Why it matters: cut points lie on edges and faces. Evidence: names parts of solids.

branches.skill: Areas of cross-sections
branches.new_demand: Compute the areas of cross-sections, not only name their shapes.

branches.skill: Use cross-section areas to compare volumes (Cavalieri)
branches.new_demand: Use cross-section areas in a Cavalieri comparison (advanced strand).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: computed cross-section areas become the input to Cavalieri's principle.

sets.target_skill: Identify the solid generated when a two-dimensional figure is rotated about a line

branches.skill: Rotation of a point about a center
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot picture what each point traces. Why it matters: the solid is made of those circles. Evidence: describes traced paths.

branches.skill: Cross-sections perpendicular to the axis
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not connect rotation with circular slices. Why it matters: it checks the solid named. Evidence: names those cross-sections.

branches.skill: Names of solids
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student knows the shape but not its name. Why it matters: answers name solids. Evidence: names solids.

branches.skill: Volumes of solids of rotation
branches.new_demand: Find the dimensions and volume of the solid generated.

branches.skill: Design an object as a solid of rotation
branches.new_demand: Use rotations to design objects with given dimensions.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: volumes of rotated figures are used in design.

sets.target_skill: Use geometric shapes, their measures, and their properties to describe real objects, compute with the model, and judge its assumptions

branches.skill: Volume formulas
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute with the chosen shape. Why it matters: the model is used through its formula. Evidence: uses volume formulas.

branches.skill: Radius from a circumference
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot get the radius from a measurable distance. Why it matters: real objects are often measured around. Evidence: finds radius from circumference.

branches.skill: Convert cubic units
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot express the answer in the needed unit. Why it matters: models answer real questions in real units. Evidence: converts units.

branches.skill: Judge a model against a measurement
branches.new_demand: Compare the model's result with a real measurement and refine the model.

branches.skill: Use the model to estimate mass with density
branches.new_demand: Combine a geometric model with a density to estimate a new quantity.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: a judged and refined model is used to estimate mass.

sets.target_skill: Compute and use densities based on area (people per square mile, trees per square kilometer) in modeling situations

branches.skill: Unit rates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot divide to get "per one". Why it matters: density is a unit rate. Evidence: computes unit rates.

branches.skill: Areas of rectangles and circles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the region's area. Why it matters: density divides by it. Evidence: computes areas.

branches.skill: Compare ratios
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student compares totals instead of rates. Why it matters: comparisons need densities. Evidence: compares rates.

branches.skill: Convert area units in density problems
branches.new_demand: Work across area units and rescale densities.

branches.skill: Plan capacity from an area density
branches.new_demand: Use area densities to set design limits.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: rescaled densities feed capacity decisions.

sets.target_skill: Compute and use densities based on volume (mass per volume, energy per volume, organisms per volume) in modeling situations

branches.skill: Volume of prisms and cylinders
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the volume. Why it matters: density uses it. Evidence: computes volumes.

branches.skill: Unit rates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student divides in the wrong order. Why it matters: density is per unit of volume. Evidence: computes and uses rates.

branches.skill: Products of numbers in scientific notation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot handle large counts. Why it matters: organism densities are large. Evidence: multiplies in scientific notation.

branches.skill: Use density to identify materials and find volumes
branches.new_demand: Reverse density problems: identify a material or find a volume or dimension.

branches.skill: Design within a mass limit
branches.new_demand: Turn a mass limit into a design limit on volume and dimensions.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving density for volume becomes a design check.

sets.target_skill: Apply geometric methods to design an object or structure that satisfies physical constraints (size limits, slopes, clearances)

branches.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the box dimensions. Why it matters: the design compares volumes. Evidence: computes box volumes.

branches.skill: Use the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the slanted constraint. Why it matters: ladders and ramps are right triangles. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Ratios and rates
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use the slope limit. Why it matters: ramp constraints are ratios. Evidence: uses ratios.

branches.skill: Inequalities as limits
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misreads the constraint. Why it matters: designs must satisfy limits. Evidence: translates limits to inequalities.

branches.skill: Satisfy several constraints at once
branches.new_demand: Check a design against two or more constraints together.

branches.skill: Find the best design with a function graph
branches.new_demand: Model the design with a polynomial function and find the optimum from its graph (Algebra II).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the constraint checks become a function whose maximum is the best design.

sets.target_skill: Apply geometric methods (surface area, area, and volume) to compare designs and choose the one with the lowest cost

branches.skill: Surface area of prisms and cylinders
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the material area. Why it matters: cost depends on it. Evidence: computes surface areas.

branches.skill: Areas of surfaces with openings
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the area that needs material. Why it matters: cost is area × unit price. Evidence: finds areas with openings.

branches.skill: Unit prices and rounding up purchases
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student rounds down purchases. Why it matters: real cost uses whole units. Evidence: rounds up correctly.

branches.skill: Compare designs with equal volume for least material
branches.new_demand: Compare several designs under a fixed requirement and choose the one using the least material.

branches.skill: Decide between designs using expected cost
branches.new_demand: Use probability to compare design costs that include risk (Probability & Statistics).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the least-material design is re-examined when failures carry a cost.

sets.target_skill: Apply ratios and measurement to lay out typographic grid systems (columns, gutters, margins, and modules) that fit a page

branches.skill: Proportional reasoning with ratios
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot apply a layout ratio. Why it matters: grids are built from ratios. Evidence: uses ratios.

branches.skill: Operate with decimals
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student makes decimal errors. Why it matters: grid measurements are decimals. Evidence: adds, subtracts, multiplies and divides decimals.

branches.skill: Factors of a whole number
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not see why some column counts split evenly. Why it matters: equal column groups need factors. Evidence: finds factors.

branches.skill: Choose grids that support several layouts
branches.new_demand: Choose and use grids that allow several layouts, working backward from a required column width.

branches.skill: Scale a grid layout to a new page size
branches.new_demand: Use similarity (one scale factor) to resize a whole grid system.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: a chosen grid is resized to another format with a single scale factor.

sets.target_skill: Derive A = ½ab sin C by drawing an altitude, and use it to find areas of triangles

branches.skill: The sine ratio in a right triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot express the altitude with sine. Why it matters: the derivation needs h = b sin C. Evidence: uses the sine ratio.

branches.skill: Area of a triangle from base and height
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the starting formula. Why it matters: the new formula comes from it. Evidence: uses ½bh.

branches.skill: The included angle of two sides
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses a non-included angle. Why it matters: the formula needs the included angle. Evidence: identifies included angles.

branches.skill: Solve for a side or an angle from an area
branches.new_demand: Use the formula backward to find an angle or a side, including the two-angle case.

branches.skill: From equal areas to the Law of Sines
branches.new_demand: Use the area formula to prove a new theorem (the Law of Sines).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the area formula, now used with any pair of sides, yields the Law of Sines.

sets.target_skill: Prove the Law of Sines (a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C) using an altitude, including the obtuse case

branches.skill: Use trigonometry in right triangles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot express h with sine. Why it matters: the proof writes h twice. Evidence: uses right-triangle trigonometry.

branches.skill: The area formula ½ab sin C
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot use the area route. Why it matters: it gives a second proof. Evidence: writes the area three ways.

branches.skill: Proportions and cross-multiplying
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot rearrange the final equation. Why it matters: the law is a proportion. Evidence: rearranges products into proportions.

branches.skill: Use the Law of Sines (AAS and ASA)
branches.new_demand: Use the proved law to solve triangles from two angles and a side.

branches.skill: Surveying with the Law of Sines
branches.new_demand: Apply the law to real surveying problems.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving AAS/ASA triangles is the computation inside triangulation.

sets.target_skill: Prove the Law of Cosines (c² = a² + b² - 2ab cos C) with coordinates or an altitude, and relate it to the Pythagorean Theorem

branches.skill: The Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the right-triangle relationships. Why it matters: the altitude proof uses them twice. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: The distance formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find AB in coordinates. Why it matters: the coordinate proof starts there. Evidence: uses the distance formula.

branches.skill: Sine and cosine in a right triangle
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the coordinates of A or simplify. Why it matters: both proofs use b cos C and b sin C. Evidence: uses sine and cosine.

branches.skill: Square a binomial
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot expand. Why it matters: the middle term becomes -2ab cos C. Evidence: expands squares.

branches.skill: Use the Law of Cosines (SAS and SSS)
branches.new_demand: Use the proved law to find a side (SAS) or an angle (SSS).

branches.skill: Distances between moving objects
branches.new_demand: Apply the law to real distance problems.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: the SAS computation now models real distances.

sets.target_skill: Apply the Law of Sines to find unknown measurements, and decide how many triangles fit SSA information (the ambiguous case)

branches.skill: The Law of Sines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot set up the law. Why it matters: every problem starts with it. Evidence: writes and solves the law.

branches.skill: Inverse sine
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot recover the angle. Why it matters: SSA problems end with sin⁻¹. Evidence: uses inverse sine.

branches.skill: Triangle angle sum
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student keeps an impossible second triangle. Why it matters: the angle sum rules it out. Evidence: checks the angle sum.

branches.skill: Sine of supplementary angles
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student misses the second triangle. Why it matters: the obtuse supplement has the same sine. Evidence: uses the supplement.

branches.skill: Solve both triangles in the ambiguous case
branches.new_demand: Solve each possible triangle completely and handle obtuse and boundary cases.

branches.skill: Bearings and navigation with the Law of Sines
branches.new_demand: Model navigation sightings as triangles and solve them.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: complete triangle solutions are applied to sightings.

sets.target_skill: Apply the Law of Cosines to find unknown distances, angles, and the magnitudes of resultant forces

branches.skill: The Law of Cosines
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot set up the law. Why it matters: every problem uses it. Evidence: writes and rearranges the law.

branches.skill: Inverse cosine
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the angle. Why it matters: SSS problems end with cos⁻¹. Evidence: uses inverse cosine.

branches.skill: Angles in a parallelogram
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student uses the wrong angle. Why it matters: force and turning problems need the supplement. Evidence: finds the triangle angle.

branches.skill: Solve a triangle with both laws
branches.new_demand: Choose and combine the two laws to solve a triangle completely.

branches.skill: Velocity vectors: airspeed and wind
branches.new_demand: Treat forces and velocities as vectors (Precalculus).
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: solving triangles with both laws becomes vector addition.

sets.target_skill: Construct the tangent lines from a point outside a given circle to the circle, and justify the construction

branches.skill: Construct the midpoint of a segment
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot locate M. Why it matters: M is the center of the helper circle. Evidence: constructs midpoints.

branches.skill: Inscribed angles on a diameter
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know why the angle is right. Why it matters: the justification uses it. Evidence: applies the theorem.

branches.skill: Tangent is perpendicular to the radius
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot justify tangency. Why it matters: the construction makes PT ⊥ OT. Evidence: uses the tangent-radius relationship.

branches.skill: Prove that the two tangent segments are congruent and compute lengths
branches.new_demand: Prove a consequence of the construction and compute tangent lengths.

branches.skill: Lines of sight to the horizon
branches.new_demand: Use the tangent-radius right triangle to model lines of sight.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: tangent-length computations model the distance to the horizon.

sets.target_skill: Derive the equation of an ellipse from its foci and the constant sum of distances, and write equations from given information

branches.skill: The distance formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the distances to the foci. Why it matters: the definition adds them. Evidence: writes distance expressions.

branches.skill: Derive a circle equation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot connect to the circle derivation. Why it matters: the ellipse derivation follows the same pattern. Evidence: derives the circle equation.

branches.skill: Expand squares
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot simplify after squaring. Why it matters: the derivation expands several squares. Evidence: expands squares.

branches.skill: Read foci and axes from an ellipse equation
branches.new_demand: Reverse the derivation: read foci and axes from an equation.

branches.skill: Design with the reflective property of ellipses
branches.new_demand: Use foci locations in physical designs.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reading foci from dimensions locates design points.

sets.target_skill: Derive the equation of a hyperbola from its foci and the constant difference of distances, and write equations from given information

branches.skill: The distance formula
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot write the distances to the foci. Why it matters: the definition subtracts them. Evidence: writes distance expressions.

branches.skill: Derive an ellipse equation
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student has not seen the parallel derivation. Why it matters: the hyperbola derivation mirrors it. Evidence: derives the ellipse.

branches.skill: Absolute value as distance
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student only considers one branch. Why it matters: the difference can be positive or negative. Evidence: uses absolute value.

branches.skill: Read foci and asymptotes from a hyperbola equation
branches.new_demand: Reverse the derivation: read foci, vertices, and asymptotes from an equation.

branches.skill: Locate a position from a time difference
branches.new_demand: Use the hyperbola definition to locate positions from distance differences.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: reading a, b, c is used to model navigation.

sets.target_skill: Give an informal argument using Cavalieri's principle for the volume of a sphere (and other solid figures)

branches.skill: Cavalieri's principle for prisms and cylinders
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student does not know the principle. Why it matters: the sphere argument rests on it. Evidence: states and applies it.

branches.skill: Cross-section radius with the Pythagorean Theorem
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the slice radius. Why it matters: the hemisphere slice area needs it. Evidence: uses the Pythagorean Theorem in 3-D.

branches.skill: Volumes of cylinders and cones
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot compute the comparison solid. Why it matters: its volume becomes the hemisphere's. Evidence: computes those volumes.

branches.skill: Area of a ring
branches.rationale: Obstacle: the student cannot find the ring area. Why it matters: the comparison slice is a ring. Evidence: computes ring areas.

branches.skill: Use Cavalieri's principle for other solids
branches.new_demand: Apply the principle to solids beyond the sphere (twisted solids, pyramids and cones).

branches.skill: Model a dome as a hemispherical shell
branches.new_demand: Use the justified sphere volume in a model with density.
branches.builds_on: Builds on FORWARD 1: volumes justified by Cavalieri are used in a structural model.
